title: MIG, MPS and driver sensitivity across GPU SKUs
content:
Summary:
This working note captures a targeted hardware comparison focused on how MIG (multi-instance GPU), MPS (Multi-Process Service), and NVIDIA driver / CUDA combinations change inference latency, tail behavior, and throughput across representative cloud SKUs for A100, H100 and L40S cards. The goal is to understand operational knobs that meaningfully affect production SLOs and unit economics when running the Redwood serving runtime.

Goals:
- Measure latency p50/p95/p99 for generation workloads (short chat vs long context) across GPUs and drivers.
- Quantify throughput and per-token cost with/without MPS and with varying MIG partitions.
- Identify cases where driver/CUDA combos introduce tail jitter or kernel regressions.
- Create pragmatic recommendations for Dedicated / Private deployments (default driver, MIG guidance, MPS tradeoffs).

High-level findings (TL;DR):
- H100 consistently gives highest raw throughput for long-context workloads, but driver/CUDA choice introduces measurable tail latency variability (notably between CUDA 12.0 and 12.2 stacks).
- A100 shows the most stable tail latency across driver versions tested (525.x, 535.x), though peak throughput is lower than H100 for FP16/FP8 workloads.
- L40S is cost-attractive for small-to-medium models but exhibits higher p99 under noisy colocated tenants; enabling MPS reduced context-switch overhead but increased p95 in some cases due to resource contention inside a single MIG instance.
- MIG partitions (1/2/3-way) provide predictable throughput scaling for batch workloads but increase per-token latency for small single-request inference (chat-style).
- MPS helps throughput for many concurrent small requests but can hurt tail latency when kernel scheduling interacts poorly with CUDA driver versions older than 535.x.

Test matrix (selected):
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), NVIDIA H100 (80GB), NVIDIA L40S (48GB)
- Cloud SKUs sampled: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100), AWS p5.48xlarge (H100), GCP L4/L40S equivalent nodes, Azure ND A100_v4 family (representative)
- Driver versions: 525.105, 535.54, 540.16 (where available).
- CUDA toolkits: 11.8, 12.1, 12.2 (runtime/PE compatibility tested).
- Runtime config: Redwood serving runtime latest dev build (commit id in linked_artifacts), runtime flags toggled: --enable-mps {on,off}, --mig-config {none,1g.10gb,2g.20gb,3g}, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set per test.
- Workloads:
  - Chat-short: 16 tokens output, context 128 tokens, concurrency 1..16
  - Chat-long: 256 tokens output, context 2048 tokens, concurrency 1..8
  - Batched-generation: batch sizes 1,4,16,32 for throughput curves
- Measurement window: steady-run 10 min after warmup, 3 runs per config, capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, power draw, PCIe vs NVLink transfers.

Environment & tooling:
- System telemetry collected via telegraf + nvidia-smi + custom kernel-span exporter.
- Per-request traces from runtime (request enqueue, kernel submit, KV cache hit/miss).
- Profiling: Nsight Systems sampling for selected bad-driver cases; CUPTI traces for kernel timing breakdown.

Representative results (condensed):
- A100 (driver 525.105, CUDA 11.8): Chat-short p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=58ms at concurrency 8; stable across runs; throughput 320 tokens/s for Chat-long (single session).
- A100 (driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1): marginal throughput uptick (~+6%) for batched FP16, p99 comparable; no regressions observed.
- H100 (driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1): Chat-long throughput +28% vs A100 on same model/quantization; but p99 increased by 20-35ms in 1 of 3 runs when driver 540.16 stack used — Nsight shows occasional kernel launch serialized due to driver-level scheduling change.
- L40S (driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1): Lower cost per token for small models; p95 varies widely (±40%) when co-located noisy processes present unless MPS used.

MIG vs non-MIG findings:
- MIG 2-way on A100: batched throughput scales ~1.9x vs single-instance for large batches, but single-request p50 increases by ~12% due to smaller effective SMs per instance.
- MIG 3-way on H100: good isolation for concurrent small workloads but suffers from worse cold-start kernel overhead due to smaller instance topology; recommend only for predictably batched workloads.

MPS observations:
- With many small concurrent workers (chat-style), enabling MPS usually increases aggregate throughput and reduces context-switch overhead between CUDA contexts.
- In driver stacks <535, we observed MPS causing occasional head-of-line blocking where long kernel launches delay short one-shot kernels — manifested as p99 spikes. On 535+ stacks the behavior improved.
- MPS + MIG combination is complex and not recommended unless explicitly validated for the target workload; some cloud images have partial support and driver mismatches cause silent failures.

Driver/CUDA sensitivity notes:
- Upgrading CUDA from 11.8 -> 12.x gave performance wins on H100 FP8 paths but required driver 535+ to avoid regression in small-request latency.
- Some vendor-provided cloud images pin a driver that is known to regress kernel launch overlap; call out these images in deployment docs.

Operational recommendations:
1) Default images: For Redwood Dedicated, recommend shipping with driver 535.x + CUDA 12.1 as base for H100/A100/L40S until further testing. Include explicit fallback plan to 525.x for customers with older infra.
2) MIG policy: Use MIG only for batched or steady multi-tenant batch workloads. For chat-first products prioritize full-GPU instances for tail latency SLOs. Document mapping of model-size -> MIG partition.
3) MPS policy: Enable MPS for high-concurrency small-request workloads but gate by driver verification (535+). Add runtime feature flag so customers can opt-out per deployment.
4) Image catalog: Maintain a small compatibility matrix (driver/CUDA/GPU) in Console UI and refuse to auto-upgrade drivers on Dedicated nodes without user opt-in.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Reproduce H100 p99 spikes under driver 540.16 more deterministically; capture full Nsight traces and escalate to NVIDIA if repeatable.
- Test quantized int8/FP8 kernels with latest LLM model variants (different tokenization patterns) to see if memory-bound patterns change the MIG recommendations.
- Evaluate emerging L40S multi-tenancy behavior on GCP with node-level QoS enforced (cgroups/cpu shares + nvidia-smi power cap).

Action items:
- [Ravi] Run 3 more long-run H100 tests with 540.16 and attach Nsight captures to INF-4123 (due 2026-02-17).
- [Jun] Add driver compatibility table to the Console deployment docs and mark 525.x, 535.x supported (due 2026-02-24).
- [Ava] Draft customer-facing note on MIG vs full-GPU recommendation for chat workloads (due 2026-02-20).

Notes and provenance:
- Measurements use serving-runtime dev build at linked PR; raw CSVs live in the linked spreadsheet.
- This document is a working draft intended to inform Dedicated/Private defaults — expect edits as more long-duration runs complete.

If you want a focused slice (e.g., only long-context H100 kernel traces or MIG cost-models for Dedicated pricing), call out the exact model/config and I'll produce the targeted report and cost delta table.
